+# Contributing to tanda
+
+Thanks for helping. tanda is small on purpose, and these rules keep it that way.
+
+## Ground rules
+
+- **No new runtime dependencies.** Standard library only, Python 3.11+. Dev-only tools need a good reason.
+- **Small PRs.** One change per PR. If it touches the queue schema, the state model or role permissions, open an issue first.
+- **Add a test with every behavior change.** For bug fixes, add a test that fails without the fix and passes with it. This is the bar tanda's own reviewer role uses.
+- **Keep the philosophy:** agents report only through the CLI, HOLD for a human by default, no idle token burn, nothing writes to GitHub without a human.
+- **Disclose AI involvement.** If a coding agent helped, say so in the PR description. That's expected and fine here.
+
+## Dev setup
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/pcbeingused333/tanda && cd tanda
+python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
+pip install -e .
+python -m unittest discover -s tests -v     # ~20 s, runs the hello demo end to end
+```
+
+To try a change by hand:
+
+```bash
+mkdir /tmp/t && cd /tmp/t && tanda init hello && tanda run
+```
+
+## Where help is most useful
+
+- Verifying the `opencode` and `codex` presets end to end, and documenting the permission flags each one needs
+- New examples under `tanda/examples/` (see below)
+- Clearer error messages, and the `tanda check` / `tanda report` commands in [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md)
+- Windows testing
+
+## Adding an example
+
+An example is a folder with `tanda.toml` and `prompts/*.md`. It gets copied by `tanda init <name>`. A good example:
+
+- runs offline, or says clearly at the top of `tanda.toml` which CLI and keys it needs;
+- gives every worker role `HOLD` among its verdicts;
+- never lets an agent push, comment or open PRs;
+- is covered by a test, if it can run with the fake agent.
+
+## Reporting bugs
+
+Include your `tanda.toml` (with secrets removed), the output of `tanda status`, and the relevant log from `.tanda/logs/`.

You can add items and move any item to any state from it: that is how a human triages, resolves a HOLD, or marks something done. It has no authentication; keep it on localhost. +1. **Triage before build.** Building a fix and then dropping it was the most expensive mistake in the in-house runs, so candidates are verified before a builder touches them. +2. **A strict, independent reviewer.** An independent reviewer (separate session) runs the builder's test itself. In the `oss-contrib` prompt, no test that fails on `main` means no `READY`. +3. **Volume limits.** Maintainers notice volume long before they notice quality. That's why `group_cap`, `blocked_groups` and dedup exist. +4. **Respect AI policies.** The example scout skips repos whose CONTRIBUTING or AGENTS file rejects AI-assisted contributions. +5. **Agents never write to GitHub.** They commit locally and draft. A human reads, decides and publishes. +6. **HOLD for a human by default.** When in doubt, or on any failure, the item stops and waits for a person. +7. **No idle token burn.** Agents only exist while there is work for them. +8. **Boring infrastructure.** One SQLite file, one process, the standard library. Easy to read, easy to debug. -## Contributing to open source without burning maintainers out +## Limitations -`examples/oss-contrib` encodes what we learned running this against real projects: +This is a working v0.1 prototype. Know these before you rely on it: -- **Triage before build.** Everything the scout finds lands in `TRIAGE` and waits for you (or an optional triage role). In our runs more candidates were dropped than published, and dropping them after a build was the most expensive mistake. -- **A strict, independent reviewer.** Every build has to show a test that fails without the fix and passes with it, before a human sees it. -- **Volume limits.** `group_cap` caps active items per repo, and `blocked_groups` skips orgs entirely. Maintainers notice volume long before they notice quality. -- **Respect AI policies.** The scout skips repos whose CONTRIBUTING/AGENTS file rejects AI-assisted contributions. -- **Agents never write to GitHub.** They commit locally and draft the PR text with a neutral disclosure; you read it, decide and publish. +- **One machine only.** The queue is a local SQLite file and there's no distributed worker support. +- **`tanda stop` does not interrupt a running `once` role.** The run waits until the scout exits. +- **The dashboard has no authentication.** Keep it on `127.0.0.1`. +- **Role permissions are a guardrail, not a sandbox.** They're enforced through `TANDA_ROLE` in the agent's environment, so an agent that runs arbitrary shell commands could get around them. Isolation (worktrees, containers, narrow agent permissions) is up to you. +- **The review gate lives in prompts.** tanda enforces *who* may set `READY` and from which state. That the reviewer actually re-ran a failing test is the reviewer prompt's job, not code. +- **No cost or token accounting yet.** `runs` records start, end, exit code and log path only. +- **Only the `claude` preset has been tested end to end.** +- **The prompt is passed as one command-line argument**, so very long prompts can hit OS argument-length limits, especially on Windows. -The in-house system these lessons come from, with its numbers, is described in [docs/case-study-oss.md](docs/case-study-oss.md). +## Roadmap + +Small, incremental, and without giving up zero dependencies. Known gaps: `tanda stop` does not interrupt a running `once` role; one machine only; the UI has no auth. Ideas and PRs are welcome. +Issues and small PRs are welcome. +# Roadmap: small improvements
+
+Concrete, small changes that would make the public version easier to use without changing its
+philosophy. That philosophy: zero dependencies, agents report only through the CLI, HOLD by
+default, no idle token burn, a human publishes. Each item is meant to fit in one small PR with
+a test.
+
+## CLI UX
+
+| # | Change | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `tanda --version` | Not there today. Makes bug reports easier. |
+| 2 | `tanda check`: validate `tanda.toml` | Catch at load time: a claimed state that no role or `initial_state` ever produces, a missing prompt file, `working` reused by two roles, a verdict with no claimant that isn't `DONE`/`DROPPED`/`HOLD`/an `extra_state`, or an agent binary not on `PATH` (`shutil.which`). |
+| 3 | `tanda init --list` and `tanda init <ex> <dir>` | You can't discover examples today without reading the source. |
+| 4 | `tanda run --dry-run` | Print each role's rendered prompt and command line without starting agents. |
+| 5 | `tanda list --group owner/repo`, `--json` | Easier scripting and triage. |
+| 6 | `tanda reset <id>` (human only) | Move a stuck `working` item back to its claim state, with an event. |
+
+## Error messages
+
+| # | Today | Better |
+|---|---|---|
+| 7 | `tanda: builder can only set BUILT DROPPED HOLD` | Add the item and a hint: `tanda: role builder cannot set READY on #12 (allowed: BUILT DROPPED HOLD)` |
+| 8 | Agent binary missing: written only to the log, then the item goes to HOLD | Also print it on the console once per role and fail fast before the run starts (with #2). |
+| 9 | The UI's `/api/set` accepts any state string | Validate it against `cfg.states` the way the CLI does, and return 400 with the valid list. |
+| 10 | `tanda ui --host 0.0.0.0` starts silently | Print a warning that the dashboard has no authentication. |
+
+## Observability
+
+| # | Change | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| 11 | `tanda report`: per-run summary from `events` | Throughput by state, verdicts per role, FIX loop count per item, HOLD reasons, median time in state. Everything needed is already in the DB. |
+| 12 | Store `run_id` on events | Tie each verdict to the agent invocation and log that produced it. |
+| 13 | Optional usage capture | If an agent prints usage JSON (for example `claude -p --output-format json`), parse tokens and cost into `runs`. Opt-in per agent, no dependency. |
+| 14 | `max_cost_per_item` (with #13) | A per-item cap, which the in-house system already has. Over the cap, the item goes to HOLD. |
+| 15 | UI: show `fields` and the reviewer's note on the card | Faster triage of `READY` and `HOLD`. |
+
+## Robustness
+
+| # | Change | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| 16 | `tanda stop` also terminates running `once` roles | A documented known gap. |
+| 17 | Pass long prompts through a file or stdin (opt-in `{prompt_file}` placeholder) | Avoids OS argument-length limits, especially on Windows. |
+| 18 | On startup, put orphaned `working` items (from a crashed run) into HOLD | Today they stay in `working` and block the "drained" condition. |
+
+## CI and packaging
+
+| # | Change |
+|---|---|
+| 19 | GitHub Actions: `python -m unittest` on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 × ubuntu, macos and windows |
+| 20 | A test per example: `tanda init <ex>` loads and passes `tanda check` |
+| 21 | Publish to PyPI so `pip install tanda` / `pipx install tanda` works, if the name is free |
+| 22 | A short screencast GIF of the hello demo in the README |
+
+## Examples
+
+| # | Example | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| 23 | `bug-bash`: one local repo, no GitHub | The scout reads `TODO`/`FIXME` and failing tests, builders fix in worktrees, the reviewer gates. The smallest realistic demo. |
+| 24 | `docs-fix`: broken links and stale snippets | Cheap models, low risk. Good for trying the opencode and codex presets. |
+| 25 | `oss-contrib`: add the optional `prompts/triage.md` | The toml refers to it, but the file isn't shipped. |
+| 26 | `hello`: let the fake agent sometimes exit without a verdict | Shows the automatic HOLD path in the demo. |
